posts.name: jorgenp
posts.cooked:
Heroic Infinitor vs. Argent Adept, Captain Cosmic, Sky-Scraper (her image isn't shown on the cover) and Chrono-Ranger in the Time Cataclysm.

 

My goodness, this one was insane!  Argent Adept has an absolutely attrocious deck order (I suggest using an early instrument card to shuffle it) and it will be a brutal slug most of the way.

I got Mint, but only barely.  I had to tank for several turns at the end with lucky draws from Sky-Scraper and even had Constructs in play as extra targets to absorb damage towards the end.  I had to wait for the final card of Infinitor's deck (Whispers of Oblivion) to get the win (as it is the easiest way to take out all the Manifestations in one foul swoop on his starting side).

The Time Cataclysm deck order is incredibly frustrating too.

 

Perhaps it would have been better to purposefully flip Infinitor?  I don't know.

 

Oh, one thing I was glad to learn:  Fixed Point does not stop Infinitor from putting cards underneath his card, thankfully.  I ended my final hero turn with only one Environment card between me and victory and I nearly had a heart attack upon seeing Fixed Point, but I still managed to win...

 

![](upload://rdq61BzTwWcTHtWTx2NkwVucTnY.jpeg)

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: Well Heroic Infinitor makes Manifestations indestructible from the get go so Fixed Point makes no difference.  Chrono was my main source of damage as I set him up on the first round to get Masadah and a Temporal Grenade through a Micro Assembler.   Then on the next round played a Sudden Contract and had Dynamic Siphon and Autonomous Blade on him so he could laying into the Manifestatioms.   The Temporal Grenade came in handy so I could quickly deal with a Surprise Shopping Trip.  All heroes (Infinitor included) ended the game in the teens.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Mint.

Well, that was close.  I ended the game with Fixed Point in play, on Infinitor's last card.  If I had reordered the damage, I could have won with Chrono at 1, and everyone else 0 or below.  When Cosmic Crest is tanking Twisted Miscreations by virtue of being the highest HP hero target, you know you're dangerously low on health.

 

Also, have I mentioned how much I love Heroic Infinitor's victory pose?  I find it hilarious for some reason.

 

Also, Heroic Infinitor, Kaargra Warfang, and Gloomweaver are the only villains that can be defeated while Fixed Point is in play.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

I probably didn't play Arget Adept optimally (I rarely feel like I do), but I used him as a healing machine. Harp, Inspiring Supertonics, and Rhapsody of Vigor with Dynamic Siphon kept everyone's HP up (including Infinitor's).

 

Cosmic Crest was helpful, it was fun playing Compulsion Canisters to have Manifestations damage each other, and Chrono-Ranger used the Masadah.

 

Like others, it was the last card in Infinitor's deck that ended it. 

 

All heroes left with either 7 or 8 HP. (even Infinitor!)
